lines.trans: Rumors are flying that she is at some luxury hotel in Paris, yet here she sits wrapping rice in seaweed!
Turns out this apartment was the five-star hotel all along!
Normally I am not allowed to eat salty, spicy food like this—who made this stew?
Who else—I cooked it.
It is truly delicious!
Really? Eat plenty!
When I asked earlier, there were no lentils, chia seeds, feta cheese, or quinoa, so today I have no choice except to eat this.
I would appreciate it if you stocked them for tomorrow—I must not consume sodium like this.
Wait—you plan on staying tomorrow too?!

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

examples.trans: Normally I am not allowed to eat salty, spicy food like this—who made this stew?

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.en: to arise, to come up, to occur
meanings.note: Used with feelings, thoughts, or events (e.g. 실감이 나다, 생각이 나다).

examples.trans: A good idea came to mind.
Tears suddenly came to my eyes.

examples.text: 내일은 좀 준비를 해주시면 감사하겠어요. 저 이렇게 나트륨 섭취하면 안 돼요.
examples.trans: I would appreciate it if you stocked them for tomorrow—I must not consume sodium like this.
This point about sodium is really important.
Did you hear about this tomorrow?
I was busy today because of tomorrow.

meanings.note: interrogative pronoun; becomes 누가 before subject particle -가

examples.trans: Did someone come outside?
Who is that person?
Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

examples.text: 뭐 해주실 거예요? 저는 페타치즈랑 렌틸콩만 있으면 돼요, 아 퀴노아랑!
examples.trans: What are you making for us? All I need is feta cheese and lentils—oh, and quinoa!

examples.text: 아까 물어보니까 렌틸콩도 없고 치아시드도 페타치즈도 퀴노아도 없다고 해서 오늘은 어쩔 수 없이 먹는데요.
examples.trans: When I asked earlier, there were no lentils, chia seeds, feta cheese, or quinoa, so today I have no choice except to eat this.

meanings.en: a lot, much, in large quantity
meanings.note: Adverbial form of 많다 (to be many/much)

examples.trans: I did a lot of work today.
Please eat plenty and enjoy.

meanings.note: Literally 'to have taste' (맛 + 있다). Pronounced [마싣따] or [마딛따].

examples.trans: The kimchi is really delicious.
The bread I ate yesterday was delicious.

examples.text: 저 원래 이런 짜고 매운 거 먹으면 안 돼요. 이거 누가 끓인 거예요?
examples.trans: Normally I am not allowed to eat salty, spicy food like this—who made this stew?
It is really spicy compared to what I expected.

meanings.note: Everyday verb for eating a meal or food; honorific equivalent is 드시다.

examples.trans: Let's eat lunch together.
Did you eat breakfast?

meanings.note: Placed directly before a noun in questions

examples.trans: What kind of music are you listening to right now?
Is something the matter?
I want to ask right now.
How about trying to ask together tomorrow?

meanings.note: By extension, refers to a meal in everyday expressions like 밥 먹다 ('to eat a meal').

examples.trans: Have you eaten?
Today's lunch is delicious.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

examples.text: 내일은 좀 준비를 해주시면 감사하겠어요. 저 이렇게 나트륨 섭취하면 안 돼요.
examples.trans: I would appreciate it if you stocked them for tomorrow—I must not consume sodium like this.
Let us do that (if I consume) right away.
Is that rumour true?
A strange rumour is going around the company.

meanings.note: Bound noun used in -(으)ㄹ 수 있다/없다 ('can / cannot').

examples.trans: I can read Korean.
I cannot go today.

meanings.en: to wrap, to pack (food to go)
meanings.note: Frequently used as 싸주다 ('to pack up for someone') when ordering takeout.

examples.trans: Please pack it to go.
I pack a lunchbox.

meanings.en: earlier, a short while ago (same day)

examples.trans: I called earlier.
What did you say earlier?

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.
Please sit on the chair.
I sat on the floor.

없다.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: to not exist, to not be present

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.
The tickets are all sold out, so there aren't any.

meanings.note: Often used directly without a locative particle to mean 'here'.

examples.trans: Please sit here.
Here is our office.

meanings.note: The present day; often used adverbially without a particle.

examples.trans: The weather is nice today.
What day of the week is it today?

meanings.note: refers to an initial state or plan

examples.trans: Traffic is usually heavy on Mondays.
This place was originally a park.
How much is this?
Please look at this.

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)

meanings.note: Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?

meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
